title: Sample call rate

blocks.what_we_do: We keep only samples with a call rate of at least 98%. We apply this rule after the rough cleaning.
blocks.why:
The call rate of a sample is the share of its sites that were read successfully. A threshold (cut-off value) of 98% means at most 2% missing results. It does not mean 98% missing results.

A sample with a low call rate gives less information. This reduces the effective sample size, which is the amount of usable data. A low call rate can also be linked to a laboratory group or a recruitment group.

In another study, look at the distribution of call rates before you choose a threshold.
blocks.you_need: State 3.1 and the call-rate definition from step 2.4.
blocks.command:
```{r s3-2}
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.1"), "--mind", "0.02", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.2")))
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.2", "3.1")
guided_register(cfg, "3.2", "3.1", 1971, 296360, operations = ops)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s3-1_state --mind 0.02 --make-pgen --out results/guided/s3-2_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--mind 0.02` removes samples with more than 2% missing calls. This is the same as a call rate below 98%. `--pfile`, `--make-pgen`, `--out`, `--threads` and `--memory` have the meanings given at step 3.1.
blocks.expected_result:
42 more wells are removed. 1,971 samples and 296,360 variants remain.



The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows. Your numbers should be the same.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the input file named in the message and the previous step. Keep the command and the console messages. Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: Moderate sample failures that the rough screen did not catch. Missingness can be linked to the [phenotype](../docs/glossary.md#phenotype), here case or control status (a case has the disease, a control does not). It can also be linked to a [batch](../docs/glossary.md#batch-effect), which is a group of samples processed together. For this reason, write down every exclusion.
blocks.quick_check:
A well has 1% missing calls. What is its call rate? Does it pass this rule?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

The call rate is 99%. The well passes the 98% call-rate rule.

</details>
blocks.files_created: `s3-2_state.*`, the list of removed samples and the replay metadata.

setup_code:
start_dir <- setwd(if (file.exists("config.R")) "." else "..")
if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = getwd())
source("R/guided.R")
cfg <- guided_init()
setwd(start_dir)

r_commands.label: s3-2
r_commands.code:
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "3.1"), "--mind", "0.02", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "3.2")))
ops <- guided_replay_lists(cfg, "3.2", "3.1")
guided_register(cfg, "3.2", "3.1", 1971, 296360, operations = ops)

options.name: --make-pgen
options.explanation_markdown: `--make-pgen` saves the result as a new fileset (a saved state).

options.name: --memory
options.explanation_markdown: `--memory 2048` sets the memory limit to 2048 MiB (about 2 gigabytes).

options.name: --mind
options.explanation_markdown: `--mind 0.02` removes samples with more than 2% missing calls.

options.name: --out
options.explanation_markdown: `--out` sets the name prefix of the output files.

options.name: --pfile
options.explanation_markdown: `--pfile` selects the input fileset in the PLINK 2 native format.

options.name: --threads
options.explanation_markdown: `--threads 2` limits the number of worker threads (parallel jobs).
